extraction.name: LAMBADA dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for evaluating word prediction requiring a broad discourse context, consisting of narrative passages where humans can guess the final target word from the full passage but not from the last sentence alone.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were collected from the Book Corpus, then filtered using language models and human crowdsourcing. A passage was included only if two consecutive human subjects could guess the target word from the whole passage and no subject could guess it from the target sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Crowdsourcing, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Narrative passages from the Book Corpus (unpublished novels); the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words before filtering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duplicate removal; filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list; exclusion of passages whose target word probability was at least 0.00175 under any of four language models; random division of novels into training and development+testing partitions; further split of development and testing by novel.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Passages were filtered to keep only those with at least 50 tokens in the context, then screened by language models and human subjects; items were discarded if they were easy for local-context language models or if they could be guessed from the target sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects on CrowdFlower guessed the target word. For each passage, one subject guessed from the whole passage; if correct, a second subject guessed from the whole passage; then additional subjects guessed from the target sentence only until the word was guessed or 10 unsuccessful guesses were reached. Only passages with two correct broad-context guesses and no correct sentence-only guess were kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors used a strict hit-or-miss inclusion criterion: two consecutive subjects had to exactly match the missing word, and no subject could guess it from local context only, even with 3 guesses. They note that allowing synonymous or plausible continuations was considered but rejected as impractical.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 human judgments per item in the filtering pipeline, and up to 12 total guesses in step 3 (10 unsuccessful guesses maximum plus the successful guess if any); step 1 and step 2 each used one subject, and step 3 used additional subjects until success or 10 failures.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Non-expert human subjects; no further demographic details reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), a 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model were used as automated filters; later experiments also used N-Gram, N-Gram with cache, RNN, LSTM, Memory Network, Sup-CBOW, and Unsup-CBOW models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus were made downloadable; the test set was to be made available at the time of a planned public competition. No further versioning, maintenance, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to stimulate research on genuine language understanding and to promote development of models that capture broad discourse phenomena.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward proper nouns and contains many items where the target word or its lemma appears in the context; quoted direct speech is overrepresented relative to the input sample.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging by design and standard language models are expected to fail on it. It is limited to English narrative passages from novels and may not generalize to other genres or domains. The authors note that the evaluation is preliminary and that better results might be obtained with more extensive tuning or more sophisticated mechanisms.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and testing of language models for broad-context word prediction; development data can be used to fine-tune models to LAMBADA-specific passages; intended as a benchmark/test set rather than a training resource for the target task.
